### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s).

**46** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfca0efb79ac5df2049f392cdecd3bbeeea9ec61`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfca0efb79ac5df2049f392cdecd3bbeeea9ec61` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b0cadad1dc48de8323409ab84244e096bf13b914` — the merge of head `05e6e0bd2330f2cc10f98d0bbb0d1e9241885529` into base `bfca0efb79ac5df2049f392cdecd3bbeeea9ec61`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b0cadad1dc48de8323409ab84244e096bf13b914 && git checkout b0cadad1dc48de8323409ab84244e096bf13b914
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bfca0efb79ac5df2049f392cdecd3bbeeea9ec61 05e6e0bd2330f2cc10f98d0bbb0d1e9241885529 && git checkout -B drift-repro bfca0efb79ac5df2049f392cdecd3bbeeea9ec61 && git merge --no-ff 05e6e0bd2330f2cc10f98d0bbb0d1e9241885529

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfca0efb79ac5df2049f392cdecd3bbeeea9ec61
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bfca0efb79ac5df2049f392cdecd3bbeeea9ec61` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8c4430f5fdf9d92204dd4f13a523f5e95d15b55a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-password-session-policy.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-plugin-list.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/organization-mfa-enrollment-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/organization-mfa-enrollment-guard.test.ts, packages/verify/src/held-session-impersonation-target.pin.test.ts, packages/verify/src/held-session-vendor-admin-doors.pin.test.ts + .changeset/30201-org-mfa-needs-enrollment.md, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-organization.object.ts (require_mfa), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/managed-extension-fields.ts (the D2 editable tier), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/identity-write-guard.ts (D2, priority 10, no object filter), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.ts (ctx.input.data precedent), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts lines 2214-2225 on main (the global mfa_required settings piece), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts applyConfigPatch and readBooleanEnv on main, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (by-id, multi-row and insert hook contexts), packages/types/src/validation-failure.ts, packages/rest/src/error-response.ts (mapDataError), packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts (ADR-0114 catalog), docs/adr/0069-enterprise-authentication-hardening.md D3, ui/packages/plugin-form/src/sanitize.ts and occSave.tsx (what the Console's edit form sends), packages/qa/dogfood/test/upgrade-harness fixtures (stored require_mfa rows), scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs and scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (the declaration readers).

Inputs read: card #30201 body and all four comments (6648424134, 6648643507, 6650356190, 6650376678); PR #30293 body, file list and the net diff against main at merge-base bb86ff96 (10 files, +692/-12); the check-runs on this head. Check-runs at judgement (05:29:46Z, after a ten-minute wait from 05:18Z): 32 success, 13 skipped, 0 failure; still in progress: Test Core (1/8) and Test Core (3/8). Every other required context is green (Lint and Repo Gates, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Test UI, Live E2E UI; Type Check UI, Lint UI and Build and E2E UI skipped by path filter; Type Check workspace, consumer, source and debt gates success; Test Core shards 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 success). The landing still waits on the two shards; this record judges the diff.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set change, the one narrowing. On a deployment where two-factor is off (resolveTwoFactorEnabled: OS_AUTH_TWO_FACTOR env, then plugins.twoFactor, then off), a write to sys_organization whose payload sets require_mfa to anything but false, 0, '0', 'false', null or undefined is refused. Right: the card's own fallback, and the value an administrator could save before is the one that produced the whole-tenant lockout.

Doors, read in the tree, each right:
- REST data API by-id PATCH and the Setup organization form (the Console's generic record editor, which sends dirty fields through dataSource.update): ObjectQL by-id update builds one hookContext with input.data = the persist image (engine.ts near line 9220); the D2 identity-write guard at priority 10 admits a user-context write of a whitelisted column (require_mfa is in MANAGED_EXTENSION_EDITABLE_FIELDS for sys_organization), then this guard at 15 judges it. Pinned on a real SQLite engine with the real SysOrganization and the real D2 guard.
- Multi-row update (where plus multi): dispatchUnscopedMultiWriteHooks and dispatchPerRowBeforeHooks both carry the same hookContext whose input.data is the shared payload (engine.ts near lines 9526 and 9566), so one judgement covers every matched row. Pinned.
- Insert: the per-row beforeInsert context carries input.data (engine.ts near line 7626); a user-context insert of sys_organization is already refused by D2 at 10, a system insert reaches this guard. Pinned.
- System context: judged, not bypassed. Right, and deliberate (the lockout does not depend on who wrote the row); the last-admin guard is the precedent.
- Metadata or Setup edit outside the data API: sys_organization is a data object, there is no metadata door for its rows; the Setup form is the data API door above.
- Not covered and not needed: raw SQL restores (the upgrade-harness fixtures load database.sql directly; their stored rows carry require_mfa = 0).

Gate fail-safe. resolveUserAuthGates now holds a user for MFA only while mfaRequired and unenrolled and isTwoFactorEnabled(); otherwise it calls noteMfaRequirementWithoutEnrollment() (one warn per manager naming the remedy) and neither holds nor stamps mfa_required_at. Right: the hold answered MFA_REQUIRED to a user whose remediation endpoint did not exist; the twoFactor plugin is pushed directly into the better-auth plugin list (auth-manager-plugin-list.ts line 271, not through addOptionalPlugin), so config on means the endpoint is wired and the four readers (plugin list, features.twoFactor, gate, guard) cannot disagree. Enrolled users were never held and still are not.

Response code and shape. validationFailure from @objectstack/types builds name ValidationError, code VALIDATION_FAILED, one fields[] entry { field: 'require_mfa', code: 'invalid_value' }; mapDataError in packages/rest keys 400 on that code; invalid_value is a member of the closed ADR-0114 catalog (errors.zod.ts line 285). Right.

Public surface. resolveTwoFactorEnabled is exported from auth-manager.ts but not re-exported from index.ts (the named list is unchanged), right. AuthManager.isTwoFactorEnabled() is a NEW public method on a class index.ts does export, so the published surface of @objectstack/plugin-auth gains one method; the PR body's "No published export ... is added; nothing is widened" misses it. A should-fix on the prose (or mark the method internal), not a semver change: the narrowing arm already carries the BREAKING banner, and an additive method on a patch-level narrowing changes no level.

### ② Semver level

Changeset .changeset/30201-org-mfa-needs-enrollment.md: @objectstack/plugin-auth patch, summary line with the ! marker, a BREAKING banner naming the accept-set narrowing, Before / Now / The gate / One answer / Unchanged, and a Remedy paragraph. Level is right by the Post-Task Checklist rule: Metadata-protocol none (sys_organization.require_mfa is a data row value, nothing a metadata author writes changes) takes patch; a non-protocol narrowing ships patch and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition, which it does.

Declaration lines. PR body and changeset both read Clause-②: no (narrowing) and Metadata-protocol: none; the one reader (scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs) reads the value and the arm, and Check Changeset is green. The two Clause-② lines are not byte-identical beyond the value: the body's tail ends "No published export, error code or settings key is added; nothing is widened." and the changeset's ends "Nothing is widened." Should-fix, cosmetic: make the tails one sentence (and drop the "no published export" claim, see ① on isTwoFactorEnabled).

ADR-0087 marker: exactly one HTML-comment marker, adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription), a spelling check-adr-0087-registration.mjs recognises (its line 931). The justification holds against the tree: no spec key, export, stored shape or stored row is removed, renamed, rewritten or dropped; the remedy is a deployment setting (OS_AUTH_TWO_FACTOR or auth.mfa_required), which no migration ledger can derive; the other categories are closed on facts the diff shows (the package publishes, no ADR-0087 id, no export removed or retyped). Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Clause-② re-declared no (narrowing) against the Claim's no: right, the dev's measurement of route (a) holds in the tree (plugin-list membership is process config re-applied at boot; nothing that builds the plugin list reads organization rows), so the refusal is the only route that survives a restart and a second node. The claim correction 6650376678 accepts it subject to this review.
- Two packages/verify pins outside the claimed surface, one key each (plugins: { twoFactor: true } beside mfaRequired). The edits do not weaken the pins: each still arms the MFA_REQUIRED posture and asserts the 403, the code and the effect never landing; two-factor on is now the only configuration in which the hold they pin exists. Should-fix, test fragility introduced by the fail-safe: in held-session-vendor-admin-doors.pin.test.ts the describe "a hold only the session's organization declares" (line 333) arms nothing of its own; its ql.update(require_mfa: true) and its expectArmed(MFA_REQUIRED) both pass only because the earlier HELD_STATES arm (line 260) left plugins.twoFactor true in the manager (its disarm at line 265 resets mfaRequired alone). Run alone or reordered, that block now fails on this head. It should arm plugins.twoFactor itself in its beforeAll. held-session-impersonation-target has no such dependent block (disarmMfa leaves twoFactor on, nothing later asserts it off).
- Skills-docs follow-up (content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx, the mfa_required row): with this head the sentence "also settable per organization via require_mfa" is wrong on a two-factor-off deployment; should-fix, carried by the seat as the report says; also docs/HARDENING.md line 242 reads the same way.
- Route (a) not taken: answered in ① and ④.
- dispatch-gates without paths; unlocked dogfood and verify builds; the depth-1 fetch; the recreated commits with the model-free trailer pair: process notes, none touches the diff.
- main moved 20 commits after the pre-PR merge, none in plugin-auth or packages/verify: the seat re-pulls before landing; the two Test Core shards still running are the only open CI state.
- Write budget 6, not 3: accounted (four pushes, one pr_create, one comment).
- open_questions: none in the report; none left by this review.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on main. ADR-0069 D3 declares the per-organization capability as "an org may require MFA above the global floor", with the mechanism row for mfa_required resting on the twoFactor plugin ("twoFactor plugin already provides TOTP"), and its hard constraint (ADR-0049, line 10) says a Require-MFA toggle that does not actually block is worse than nothing. On main the organization toggle met neither half honestly: it blocked everyone, and the enrollment half of D3's mechanism was absent, so what the consumer had was not the declared capability but a lockout. This diff takes nothing the spec declares away at the consumer: the org still tightens above the floor whenever the floor's own mechanism (the twoFactor plugin) is present, and it makes the spec's own precondition real by refusing the write when it is not, with the remedy in the refusal. The gate fail-safe is the same reading applied to rows that already exist. PASS on the design, with the findings below, none must-fix.

Breaking attempts:
- Two-factor turned OFF after organizations saved require_mfa = true (global switch turned off then restarted, or an env pin): no lockout; the gate warns once and holds nobody; the row keeps true, so the organization form and GET /api/v1/data/sys_organization still show Require Multi-Factor Auth ticked while features.twoFactor is false. Nothing on the read side says "not enforced". Should-fix (the domain:ui half already listed for the seat, plus the API: a reader has to join two surfaces to learn the truth). Not a must-fix here: the write door now refuses the lie going forward, the server says so in the log, and the alternative was the lockout.
- OS_AUTH_TWO_FACTOR=false pinned: the org write is refused, right; the global auth.mfa_required setting still saves and shows on while the gate does not enforce it (the PR's acceptance note). Two should-fixes, same file surface: (i) the refusal message's second remedy, "turn on the auth.mfa_required setting, which ... turns enrollment on with it", is false under exactly this pin, since the env outranks the settings patch (readBooleanEnv first in resolveTwoFactorEnabled); under a pin the only remedy is the env, and the message should say so or drop the second remedy when the env is set. (ii) the settings piece at auth-plugin.ts line 2220 could refuse mfa_required = true the same way this guard refuses the org write when the env pins two-factor off, instead of saving an unenforced switch; pre-existing shape, not introduced here.
- OS_AUTH_TWO_FACTOR=true pinned: plugin list, features, gate and guard all read true; every write admitted, every unenrolled member held after grace. Holds.
- Global mfa_required interplay: on turns plugins.twoFactor on in the same refusable patch, so org writes are admitted from then on and a stored org row starts holding; off patches mfaRequired alone, twoFactor stays on in-process until restart, so held members stay held and still can enroll until the next boot, when the settings pass no longer turns two-factor on and the fail-safe takes over. No window in which a user is held without an enrollment path. Holds.
- A seeded or package-installed organization row with require_mfa = true at boot: the guard binds at kernel:ready; a system insert after that is refused with the same 400, which is a correct, located refusal of a row the deployment cannot honour (the install fails on that row with the remedy in the message), not a silent drop. Nothing in this repository seeds such a row (the three upgrade-harness fixtures store 0 and load by raw SQL, so no hook runs). Holds.
- Multi-node: the guard and the gate read the node's own config; the settings pass runs on every node at boot, and a runtime settings change propagates exactly as every other auth setting does today (not by this diff). A node where two-factor is on holds and admits writes, a node where it is off neither holds nor admits them; no node holds a user it cannot enroll. Holds; the cross-node settings lag is pre-existing and out of scope.
- mfa_required_at no longer stamped while two-factor is off: its readers on main are the gate itself and documentation (the QA checklist describes the lazy stamp); no code reads it elsewhere. Consequence pinned by the diff's own e2e: a user stamped during the old dead end is held the moment two-factor turns on (the stamp is older than the window) and POST /two-factor/enable answers 200 for that held session, so the hold is now compliable. A user never stamped gets a fresh window when enrollment opens. Holds; the "held at once" case is a disclosed, correct outcome, since the window existed to allow enrollment and the user could not enroll then.
- Judged on the payload, not on the transition. A writer that re-sends a stored require_mfa = true unchanged on a two-factor-off deployment is refused, with a message saying the organization "cannot require multi-factor authentication yet" although the row already says it does: full-row clients (an SDK or MCP update that echoes the record, an import re-run) and the Console's no-change save (dirtyEditPayload falls back to the whole payload when nothing changed) cannot touch such an organization until they untick the box or turn two-factor on. The by-id context carries previous, so an unchanged true could pass while a false-to-true transition is refused; the multi-row path would need the prior rows it already reads. Should-fix; not a must-fix because the Console's edit form sends only changed fields, so the card's door is unaffected, and the refusal names a real remedy.
- turnsMfaRequirementOn treats 'off' and 'no' as on (readBooleanEnv treats them as off): the column is boolean, the engine refuses those strings later anyway, and the guard's docblock says so. Not a finding.
- The refusal reaches a user-context caller only after D2 admitted the write, so a non-administrator never learns the deployment's two-factor state from this message. Holds.

Findings, each named:
- should-fix: vendor-admin-doors org-only block depends on an earlier state's leftover plugins.twoFactor (③).
- should-fix: refuse on the false-to-true transition rather than on an echoed true (④).
- should-fix: the refusal's second remedy is false under an OS_AUTH_TWO_FACTOR=false pin (④).
- should-fix: the global mfa_required settings door saves an unenforced switch under the same pin, the symmetric gap (④, pre-existing shape).
- should-fix: a stored require_mfa = true reads as required on every surface while unenforced; the UI half and an API-side signal (④).
- should-fix: PR body says no published export is added, but AuthManager.isTwoFactorEnabled() is a new public method on an exported class (①).
- should-fix: Clause-② line tails differ between PR body and changeset (②).
- should-fix: authentication.mdx and HARDENING.md still say require_mfa is settable per organization unconditionally (③).
- must-fix: none.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `05e6e0bd2330f2cc10f98d0bbb0d1e9241885529`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-password-session-policy.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-plugin-list.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/organization-mfa-enrollment-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/organization-mfa-enrollment-guard.test.ts, packages/verify/src/held-session-impersonation-target.pin.test.ts, packages/verify/src/held-session-vendor-admin-doors.pin.test.ts + .changeset/30201-org-mfa-needs-enrollment.md, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (update(): the by-id prior read, its not-found gate and the previous binding before the beforeUpdate dispatch; the predicate branch's matched-row read, hasHooksFor and the per-row dispatch before updateMany; the unscoped-multi dispatch), packages/objectql/src/engine-hook-dispatch.ts (dispatchPerRowBeforeHooks, the per-row previous binding), packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts (readUpdatePriorRow, declared columns only), packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts (update.options.upsert retired), packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts (update and upsert rows written through updateData by id), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts applyConfigPatch (plugins merged shallowly) and resolveTwoFactorEnabled over readBooleanEnv, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/managed-extension-fields.ts (require_mfa in the editable tier), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/tsup.config.ts (dts emitted, no stripInternal anywhere in the repo), packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-organization.object.ts (require_mfa declared boolean), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (the not-required categories), scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs (the declaration reader), packages/qa/dogfood/test/upgrade-harness fixtures (stored require_mfa rows).

Delta review of the head the full review passed (record 6650579682, head 8c4430f5). Inputs read: card #30201 body and its four comments; PR #30293 body as it stands and its pending replacement (server-seat2/30201/pr-body-v2.md); the file list, the net diff against main at this head (10 files, +794/-12) and the delta 8c4430f5..f643025e (6 files, +127/-25); the check-runs on this head. The range 8c4430f5..05e6e0bd holds exactly two commits: f643025e (the fix) and 05e6e0bd, one merge of main at 8b117c0e (the earlier head was itself the merge at bb86ff96, so this PR carries two main merges in all). The diff f643025e..05e6e0bd over plugin-auth, packages/verify and the changeset is empty: the merge touches no path of this PR; what it brings to packages/objectql/src/engine.ts is main's own, and every engine citation below was read at this head. Check-runs at judgement (2026-11-05T06:49Z): after five readings over ten minutes from the first at 2026-11-05T06:40Z to the last at 2026-11-05T06:49Z: 29 success, 13 skipped, 0 failure or other; still in progress: 5 (Test Core (1/8), Test Core (2/8), Test Core (3/8), Test Core (4/8), Test Core (7/8)). Green and complete: Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, every Lint job, Type Check consumer, source and debt gates, Build Core, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate; Type Check UI, Lint UI and Build and E2E UI skipped by path filter. The shards still running are the landing's wait; this record judges the diff, as the earlier one did.

### ① Derived judgments

The delta replaces the payload rule with a transition rule. Every accept-set change it makes, judged:

- A by-id update whose payload carries require_mfa on for a row that already stores it on, two-factor off: REFUSED before, PASSES now. Right. The write turns nothing on; the gate does not enforce the stored value while two-factor is off (resolveUserAuthGates, unchanged in the delta); refusing it blocked every other edit of that row through a whole-record door, which was the earlier record's should-fix. The engine binds previous unconditionally on this path (readUpdatePriorRow before the dispatch) and throws recordNotFound before any hook when the row is absent, so the guard never meets a by-id context without previous.
- A multi-row update whose payload carries on and whose every matched row stores on: REFUSED before, PASSES now. Right, same reasoning. The predicate branch reads the matched rows (readPriorRows over the composed AST and the same driver options updateMany uses) whenever hasHooksFor('beforeUpdate', object) is true, which the guard's own registration makes true, and dispatchPerRowBeforeHooks binds previous = that row, coerced, on each per-row context, all before updateMany. The dev's real-engine pin covers it (where slug acme, both rows on, lands with timezone written).
- A multi-row update with at least one matched row stored off: refused before and now, with nothing written. Right; now judged per row, and the throw from any row's chain leaves updateMany unreached. Pinned (org_a on, org_b off: refused, org_b still off, org_a's timezone not written).
- An insert with on, and a by-id update of a row stored off, null or never set: refused before and now. Right. previous.require_mfa null or absent is off, so an update that sets it is a change.
- A beforeUpdate context with no previous: refused. Right as a fail-safe; no engine path produces one (by-id: unconditional read, 404 first; predicate: per row), so it is reachable only by a hand-built context, and a context that cannot prove the prior state is not evidence the value was on.
- A multi-row update matching zero rows: zero per-row dispatches (D1) before and now; the unscoped-multi dispatch reaches only registrations that declare for it, which this guard does not. No change.
- Stored forms: previous arrives through coerceBooleanFields on both paths, and turnsMfaRequirementOn reads 1, '1', 'true' as on and 0, '0', 'false', null, undefined as off, so a SQLite 0/1 or an uncoerced string judges the same way.
- The reverse direction, a write that passed before and is refused now: none. The transition rule accepts a strict superset of the payload rule, so the narrowing declared on the earlier head is now narrower, not wider, and no new refusal appears.
- Copy: the refusal and the once-per-manager warning now offer the auth.mfa_required remedy only unless OS_AUTH_TWO_FACTOR is set to false. ### ④ Design judgment

The transition rule against the published spec on main. ADR-0069 D3 declares the per-organization requirement above the global floor on the twoFactor plugin's mechanism; the earlier record found the refusal makes that precondition real at the write door and the gate fail-safe applies the same reading to stored rows. The delta narrows the refusal to the writes that create the state the spec cannot honour and lets every write that leaves it as stored through, which is the right boundary: a value the gate does not enforce is not made more dangerous by being echoed, and refusing the echo took the row's other edits hostage. PASS on the design. Attempts to break it:

- An update path that does not bind previous. Bulk update by filter: the predicate branch reads the matched rows before the per-row dispatch whenever the object has a beforeUpdate hook, and this guard's registration is one, so previous is bound per row through the same AST and driver options updateMany then uses, and the rows judged are the rows written. Import and seed: the import runner (packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts) resolves an update or upsert row's target by its match fields and writes it with updateData by id, so a re-run echoing true passes and an off-to-on row is refused per row; insert mode goes through insert and is refused when on. Upsert: the engine's update.options.upsert is a retired key (ENGINE_UPDATE_UPSERT_REMOVED); there is no upsert door that could bypass the by-id read. Raw driver writes and raw SQL run no hooks at all: no non-test writer of require_mfa exists outside the engine at this head, the harness fixtures store 0, and this exposure is the earlier head's, unchanged by the transition rule. Holds.
- A race of two concurrent updates. previous is read before the write with no lock or precondition, as every previous-reading guard here (last-admin included). The one ordering that admits a value the rule would otherwise refuse: writer A clears true to false, writer B read true before A landed and echoes true, B passes, the row ends true with two-factor off. The outcome is a row stored true, which the gate does not enforce while two-factor is off, which holds nobody, and which the next off-to-on write is judged against; no lockout path opens. The other orderings refuse (B's previous read false after A cleared it) or admit only while two-factor is on. Holds; not a finding.
- true to false to true within one batch. A multi-row update carries one shared payload for every matched row (D3 pins the payload by reference identity), so a batch cannot carry both values; a batch insert judges each row's own payload with no previous; sequential by-id writes are each judged against the row as stored at that moment (true to false passes, false to true is refused). A hook earlier in the per-row loop that rewrote the shared payload to off would make later rows pass, which is the clearing direction and is also what the key-divergence refusal exists for. Holds.
- An update that leaves require_mfa unchanged but is judged as a change. Needs a beforeUpdate context without previous or with previous.require_mfa off while the row stores on. The by-id read is unconditional and reads declared columns of the whole row (require_mfa is declared); the predicate read is the whole matched row, declared columns only; coercion keeps a 1 as on; a row the caller's row scope hides is a 404 before any hook. None reachable. Holds.
- Ordering inside the guard: the unchanged check runs before the two-factor read, so an echoed true never consults config; the insert handler ignores a previous it is handed. Right.
